# Worker Helm chart examples

Use these worker configuration variations — ingress, intermediate, and egress topologies, DNS-based addressing, and registration methods — to adapt a worker to your network position. They assume a Boundary controller or HCP Boundary cluster already exists.

Create the namespace once before you install any of the examples:

```shell-session
$ kubectl create namespace boundary
```

The chart enables TLS for the operations listener by default. Create the default TLS Secret before you install a worker. Replace the placeholders with paths to a certificate and private key that are valid for the worker operations endpoint:

```shell-session
$ kubectl create secret tls boundary-worker-tls \
  --namespace boundary \
  --cert=<path-to-tls.crt> \
  --key=<path-to-tls.key>
```

The examples keep operations TLS enabled and use the chart's `tls.ops.disabled` and `tls.mountPath` values in the HCL. If you change `tls.secretName`, create the TLS Secret with the same name.

<Warning>

The inline AEAD (Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data) worker-auth configuration in these examples is for development and testing only. The worker-auth trust configuration must match the controllers. Use an external KMS for production deployments.

</Warning>

| Topology | Accepts connections from | Typical Service type | Needs `public_addr` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ingress | Downstream workers and clients | `LoadBalancer` | Yes |
| Intermediate | Upstream and downstream workers | `LoadBalancer` | Yes |
| Egress | Upstream or intermediate workers; connects to targets | `ClusterIP` | No |

## Worker with ingress capabilities

An ingress worker accepts connections from downstream workers and clients. It commonly uses the controller cluster as its upstream and exposes the proxy listener publicly through a `LoadBalancer` Service.

Save the following complete HCL and values as `ingress-values.yaml`:

```yaml
worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      name              = "boundary-worker"
      public_addr       = "boundary-worker.example.com:9202"
      initial_upstreams = ["boundary-controller-cluster:9201"]

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "ingress"]
      }
    }

    kms "aead" {
      purpose   = "worker-auth"
      aead_type = "aes-gcm"
      key       = "<base64-encoded-32-byte-key>"
      key_id    = "<worker-auth-key-id>"
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  service:
    proxy:
      type: LoadBalancer
      port: 9202
      targetPort: 9202
    ops:
      type: ClusterIP
      port: 9203
      targetPort: 9203
  persistence:
    authStorage:
      enabled: false
      path: /var/lib/boundary
    recording:
      enabled: false
      path: /boundary/recording
```

Install the worker Helm chart:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values ingress-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

If you do not know the `public_addr` until the load balancer is created, wait for the external address:

```shell-session
$ kubectl get svc boundary-worker-proxy --namespace boundary --watch
```

Example output:

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```
NAME                     TYPE           CLUSTER-IP     EXTERNAL-IP     PORT(S)          AGE
boundary-worker-proxy    LoadBalancer   10.0.0.30      <pending>       9202:31600/TCP   10s
boundary-worker-proxy    LoadBalancer   10.0.0.30      203.0.113.20    9202:31600/TCP   45s
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

Update `public_addr` in `ingress-values.yaml`, and then upgrade with the same values file:

```shell-session
$ helm upgrade boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values ingress-values.yaml \
  --rollback-on-failure \
  --wait
```

## Worker with intermediate capabilities

A worker with intermediate capabilities relays traffic between upstream and downstream workers. It requires both `initial_upstreams` and `public_addr`.

Save the following complete HCL and values as `intermediate-values.yaml`:

```yaml
worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      name              = "boundary-worker"
      public_addr       = "boundary-worker.example.com:9202"
      initial_upstreams = ["ingress-or-intermediate-worker.example.com:9202"]

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "intermediate"]
      }
    }

    kms "aead" {
      purpose   = "worker-auth"
      aead_type = "aes-gcm"
      key       = "<base64-encoded-32-byte-key>"
      key_id    = "<worker-auth-key-id>"
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  service:
    proxy:
      type: LoadBalancer
      port: 9202
      targetPort: 9202
    ops:
      type: ClusterIP
      port: 9203
      targetPort: 9203
  persistence:
    authStorage:
      enabled: false
      path: /var/lib/boundary
    recording:
      enabled: false
      path: /boundary/recording
```

Install the worker Helm chart:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values intermediate-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

If you do not know the `public_addr` until the load balancer is created, wait for the external address (refer to the example output shown in [Worker with ingress capabilities](#worker-with-ingress-capabilities)):

```shell-session
$ kubectl get svc boundary-worker-proxy --namespace boundary --watch
```

Update `public_addr` in `intermediate-values.yaml`, then upgrade with the same values file:

```shell-session
$ helm upgrade boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values intermediate-values.yaml \
  --rollback-on-failure \
  --wait
```

## Worker with egress capabilities

A worker with egress capabilities connects to target systems and is usually the final hop before a target. It often does not need a `public_addr`.

Both Services always render. For an egress worker, use `ClusterIP` for the proxy and operations Services. Save the following complete HCL and values as `egress-values.yaml`:

```yaml
worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      name              = "boundary-worker"
      initial_upstreams = ["ingress-or-intermediate-worker.example.com:9202"]

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "egress"]
      }
    }

    kms "aead" {
      purpose   = "worker-auth"
      aead_type = "aes-gcm"
      key       = "<base64-encoded-32-byte-key>"
      key_id    = "<worker-auth-key-id>"
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  service:
    proxy:
      type: ClusterIP
      port: 9202
      targetPort: 9202
    ops:
      type: ClusterIP
      port: 9203
      targetPort: 9203
  persistence:
    authStorage:
      enabled: false
      path: /var/lib/boundary
    recording:
      enabled: false
      path: /boundary/recording
```

Install the worker with a values file that includes the worker configuration:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values egress-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

## Worker with a pre-configured DNS address

If you already control the DNS name for the worker, set `public_addr` during installation. The address must use `host:port` format without a URL scheme. Save the following complete HCL and values as `ingress-values.yaml`:

```yaml
worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      name              = "boundary-worker"
      public_addr       = "boundary-worker.example.com:9202"
      initial_upstreams = ["boundary-controller-cluster:9201"]

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "ingress"]
      }
    }

    kms "aead" {
      purpose   = "worker-auth"
      aead_type = "aes-gcm"
      key       = "<base64-encoded-32-byte-key>"
      key_id    = "<worker-auth-key-id>"
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  service:
    proxy:
      type: LoadBalancer
      port: 9202
      targetPort: 9202
    ops:
      type: ClusterIP
      port: 9203
      targetPort: 9203
  persistence:
    authStorage:
      enabled: false
      path: /var/lib/boundary
    recording:
      enabled: false
      path: /boundary/recording
```

Install the worker Helm chart:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values ingress-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

After the Service receives an external address, point the DNS record to that address. This avoids changing the worker HCL after installation, but you remain responsible for ensuring that DNS resolves to the reachable worker endpoint.

## Worker-led registration

For worker-led registration, install the worker without a controller-generated activation token. The worker generates identity material at startup and writes registration information to the pod logs. For more information, see [Worker-led registration](/boundary/docs/workers/registration/worker-led).

Save the following complete HCL and values as `worker-values.yaml`. Worker-led registration requires persistent auth storage at `/var/lib/boundary`:

```yaml
worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      initial_upstreams = ["boundary-controller-cluster:9201"]
      auth_storage_path = "/var/lib/boundary"

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "worker-led"]
      }
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  persistence:
    authStorage:
      enabled: true
      size: 1Gi
      path: /var/lib/boundary
```

Install the worker Helm chart:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values worker-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

The typical workflow is as follows:

1. Install the worker chart with worker-led registration settings in `worker.config`.
2. Read the worker pod logs.
3. Register or authorize the emitted worker registration information with Boundary.
4. Confirm the worker becomes active.

View logs:

```shell-session
$ kubectl logs --namespace boundary deployment/boundary-worker-deployment
```

Keep auth storage enabled for worker-led registration so the generated worker identity persists across pod replacement. When `worker.persistence.authStorage.enabled` is `false`, the chart mounts an `emptyDir` at `/var/lib/boundary`, and the identity does not persist when Kubernetes replaces the pod.

## Controller-led registration

The typical workflow for controller-led registration is as follows. For more details about controller-led registration, refer to [Controller-led registration](/boundary/docs/workers/registration/controller-led):

1. Create the worker resource in Boundary or HCP Boundary.
2. Obtain the controller-generated activation token.
3. Supply the token using one of the methods below.
4. Install the worker Helm chart.
5. Confirm the worker registers and persists its credentials to auth storage.

The worker uses the activation token during initial bootstrap. After successful registration, the worker uses persisted credentials from auth storage.

The chart supports three ways to supply the activation token.

<Note>

The plaintext and `extraEnv` methods store the token in the Helm release Secret, which means it is visible to anyone who can run `helm get values boundary-worker --namespace boundary`. Use the `secretRefs` method if you need the token to stay out of Helm release storage entirely.

</Note>

### Plaintext token

Embed the token directly in `worker.config`. Suitable for development only — the token is visible to anyone who can read the ConfigMap.

Save the following complete HCL and values as `worker-values.yaml`:

```yaml
worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      name                                  = "boundary-worker"
      initial_upstreams                     = ["boundary-controller-cluster:9201"]
      auth_storage_path                     = "/var/lib/boundary"
      controller_generated_activation_token = "<activation-token>"

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "controller-led"]
      }
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  persistence:
    authStorage:
      enabled: true
      size: 1Gi
      path: /var/lib/boundary
```

Install the worker Helm chart:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values worker-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

### Token via extraEnv

Set `controller_generated_activation_token` to the `env://` reference in `worker.config` and supply the token as a key-value pair in `extraEnv`. Save the following complete HCL and values as `worker-values.yaml`:

```yaml
extraEnv:
  - name: BOUNDARY_WORKER_CONTROLLER_GENERATED_ACTIVATION_TOKEN
    value: "<activation-token>"

worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      name                                  = "boundary-worker"
      initial_upstreams                     = ["boundary-controller-cluster:9201"]
      auth_storage_path                     = "/var/lib/boundary"
      controller_generated_activation_token = "env://BOUNDARY_WORKER_CONTROLLER_GENERATED_ACTIVATION_TOKEN"

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "controller-led"]
      }
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  persistence:
    authStorage:
      enabled: true
      size: 1Gi
      path: /var/lib/boundary
```

Install the worker Helm chart:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values worker-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

### Token from a Kubernetes Secret

Store the activation token in a Kubernetes Secret and reference it using `secretRefs`. The chart injects the Secret value as the `BOUNDARY_WORKER_CONTROLLER_GENERATED_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` environment variable, which Boundary reads at startup via the `env://` prefix.

Create the Secret before installing the chart:

```shell-session
$ kubectl create secret generic boundary-worker-secrets \
  --namespace boundary \
  --from-literal=worker-controller-generated-activation-token='<activation-token>'
```

The key name (`worker-controller-generated-activation-token`) must match the value set in `secretRefs.keys.controllerGeneratedActivationToken` in your Helm values file. This command is provided as an example — use any Secret management method that fits your workflow.

Set `controller_generated_activation_token` to the exact supported `env://BOUNDARY_WORKER_CONTROLLER_GENERATED_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` reference. Save the following complete HCL and values as `worker-values.yaml`:

```yaml
secretRefs:
  secretName: boundary-worker-secrets
  validateExisting: true
  keys:
    controllerGeneratedActivationToken: worker-controller-generated-activation-token

worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      name                                  = "boundary-worker"
      initial_upstreams                     = ["boundary-controller-cluster:9201"]
      auth_storage_path                     = "/var/lib/boundary"
      controller_generated_activation_token = "env://BOUNDARY_WORKER_CONTROLLER_GENERATED_ACTIVATION_TOKEN"

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "controller-led"]
      }
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  persistence:
    authStorage:
      enabled: true
      size: 1Gi
      path: /var/lib/boundary
```

With `secretRefs.validateExisting: true`, the chart looks up the Secret during an install or upgrade and fails early when the Secret or configured key is missing. Client-only `helm template` rendering cannot find an in-cluster Secret, so use a cluster-connected install or upgrade to perform this validation.

<Note>

When `secretRefs.secretName` is set, the chart validates that `worker.config` uses the correct `env://` variable name for the secret-backed field. Using a different variable name causes the chart to fail during rendering before installation completes. The required name is:

- `env://BOUNDARY_WORKER_CONTROLLER_GENERATED_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` for `controller_generated_activation_token`

If you use a different variable name, the chart fails during rendering with an error message that identifies the field and the expected variable name. Hardcoding the token directly in `worker.config` when `secretRefs.secretName` is set is also rejected.

</Note>

Install the worker Helm chart:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values worker-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

Keep auth storage enabled at `/var/lib/boundary` for every controller-led token method so registered credentials persist across pod replacement. When `worker.persistence.authStorage.enabled` is `false`, the chart mounts an `emptyDir` at that path, and the credentials do not persist when Kubernetes replaces the pod.

## KMS (key management system)-backed worker authentication

Boundary only supports KMS-backed worker authentication in self-managed deployments. For more information, refer to [External KMS registration](/boundary/docs/workers/registration/kms). It is not available for HCP Boundary workers.

For self-managed deployments, configure the worker HCL with an external KMS worker-auth stanza that matches the controllers. The following example uses AWS KMS. Configure workload credentials that grant the pod access to the KMS key, and replace the placeholders for your environment. Save the complete HCL and values as `worker-values.yaml`:

```yaml
worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      name              = "boundary-worker"
      initial_upstreams = ["boundary-controller-cluster:9201"]

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "kms"]
      }
    }

    kms "awskms" {
      purpose    = "worker-auth"
      region     = "<aws-region>"
      kms_key_id = "<aws-kms-key-id>"
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  persistence:
    authStorage:
      enabled: false
      path: /var/lib/boundary
```

Install the worker Helm chart:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values worker-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

KMS authentication does not require persistent local auth material. When `worker.persistence.authStorage.enabled` is `false`, the chart mounts an `emptyDir` at `/var/lib/boundary` instead of creating a PVC. Data in that volume does not persist when Kubernetes replaces the pod.

## Enable session recording storage

If the worker stores session recordings, enable recording persistence and set `recording_storage_path` in `worker.config` to the same path.

<Note>

To create Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) session recording exports, the worker environment requires FFmpeg 5.1.0 or later and `libsvtav1`. Refer to [Configure worker storage](/boundary/docs/session-recording/configuration/configure-worker-storage#ffmpeg) for requirements.

</Note>

Save the following complete HCL and values as `worker-values.yaml`:

```yaml
worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9202"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      name                   = "boundary-worker"
      initial_upstreams      = ["boundary-controller-cluster:9201"]
      recording_storage_path = "/boundary/recording"

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "recording"]
      }
    }

    kms "aead" {
      purpose   = "worker-auth"
      aead_type = "aes-gcm"
      key       = "<base64-encoded-32-byte-key>"
      key_id    = "<worker-auth-key-id>"
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  persistence:
    recording:
      enabled: true
      size: 10Gi
      path: /boundary/recording
```

Install the worker Helm chart:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values worker-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

Ensure the recording storage path in `worker.config` matches `worker.persistence.recording.path`.

## Change service ports

You can change the proxy listener port when the HCL listener address and `worker.service.proxy.targetPort` match. Save the following complete HCL and values as `worker-values.yaml`:

```yaml
worker:
  config: |
    disable_mlock = true

    listener "tcp" {
      address = "0.0.0.0:9222"
      purpose = "proxy"
    }

    listener "tcp" {
      address       = "0.0.0.0:9203"
      purpose       = "ops"
      tls_disable   = "{{ .Values.tls.ops.disabled }}"
      tls_cert_file = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.crt"
      tls_key_file  = "{{ .Values.tls.mountPath }}/tls.key"
    }

    worker {
      name              = "boundary-worker"
      public_addr       = "boundary-worker.example.com:9222"
      initial_upstreams = ["boundary-controller-cluster:9201"]

      tags {
        type = ["worker", "ingress"]
      }
    }

    kms "aead" {
      purpose   = "worker-auth"
      aead_type = "aes-gcm"
      key       = "<base64-encoded-32-byte-key>"
      key_id    = "<worker-auth-key-id>"
    }

    events {
      audit_enabled        = true
      sysevents_enabled    = true
      observations_enabled = true
      sink "stderr" {
        name        = "all-events"
        event_types = ["*"]
        format      = "cloudevents-json"
      }
    }
  service:
    proxy:
      port: 9222
      targetPort: 9222
    ops:
      port: 9443
      targetPort: 9203
```

Install the worker Helm chart:

```shell-session
$ helm install boundary-worker hashicorp/boundary-worker \
  --namespace boundary \
  --values worker-values.yaml \
  --wait
```

The chart does not synchronize proxy settings automatically. The operations listener and `worker.service.ops.targetPort` must remain `9203` because the Deployment's named operations container port and health probes are hardcoded to 9203. You can change the Service-facing `worker.service.ops.port`, as the example shows.

## Troubleshooting

### Session recordings fail to export

If session recording exports fail, confirm that the worker environment provides FFmpeg 5.1.0 or later and the `libsvtav1` codec, as described in [Enable session recording storage](#enable-session-recording-storage).

## More information

To view supported Helm values so that you can configure or update workers, refer to [Worker values](/boundary/docs/deploy/helm-chart/worker-values).
